name: Template dashboard
purpose: A PAGE-SCALE ORGANISM for an overview screen: a page header lock-up, a board of Kpi-tiles, a chart panel beside a summary rail, and a Data-grid of recent records. Its question is 'how are things, and what needs me?', which is a question about SEVERAL records at once — that is what separates it from the detail template. Composed entirely from existing components; the only new CSS is thirteen composition rules, each a relationship between panels.
$status: PROPOSED #210 under the WAVE-5 Layer-2 fan-out brief (notes/_briefs/2026-08-20-210-wave5-layer2-p2-fanout-brief-v1.md, LANE B). ⛔ NOT GATED, NOT RULED, NOT REGISTERED — absent from CATEGORIES, MIGRATED_SNIPPETS, component-types.json, canon.css, gen_showroom.py and _rulings.json. Dave's eye is owed on every semantic below.
$artefactClass: The Layer-2 artefact class is itself a PROPOSED convention, stated once in the brief: Layer-2 rows have no ruled artefact form, so each ships in the SAME grammar as the component library — knowledge/snippets/<Name>.reference.html + knowledge/components/<slug>.meta.json with a `layer` field — because the one grammar keeps every existing gate watching these files for free, where a parallel pipeline would be born ungated. Dave may re-home the class.
$cardinalRule: COMPOSE, NEVER RE-DRAW. Every visible atom traces to a source component file and every borrowed region is diff-proven in notes/_receipts/2026-08-20-210-wave5-laneB-templates.md. The Meter precedent (s210-D1) is the model: zero new CSS is the ideal, a COMPOSITION class is legal, a re-drawn atom is the #202 defect.

accessibility.landmarks: The template is the CONTENT REGION of a page and renders inside a single <main>. The app frame (top nav / side nav / multi-column) is itinerary rows 97/98/99 and is a separate artefact class; the relationship is PROPOSED, not adjudicated.
accessibility.headingOrder: One <h1> (the page title). Section titles are <h2>, panel titles <h3>. The .t-cm-section-label composite is a TYPE class and never substitutes for a heading element.
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: Every RAG chip carries its word; the dot is decorative and aria-hidden. Table selection is tint + an inset start bar + a checked box. Sparkline trend is declared as data-trend as well as coloured. (1.4.1)
accessibility.reducedMotion: Every borrowed region brings its own prefers-reduced-motion override, plus the page-level kill. (2.3.3)
accessibility.reflow: Proven by DRIVING at 1400 / 820 / 420 CSS px in light and dark: zero horizontal page overflow at every width. Wide, fixed-canvas regions (the chart, the table) scroll INSIDE their own region rather than the page. (1.4.10)
accessibility.targetSize: ⚠ DECLARED, NOT CLAIMED. Buttons, tabs, pager cells and row download controls measure ≥ 44px. THREE INHERITED SHORTFALLS ARE MEASURED AND REPORTED, NOT SILENTLY FIXED: Breadcrumbs' .crumb links measure 39.4x10.1 (the leading-trim cap box is the link box); View-options' .seg buttons are 40px tall; Data-grid's .dgs-clear and .fchip .x are 24x24. All three are the SOURCE components' shipped geometry and are Dave's to rule. The a11y gate reports the first as 'UNMEASURED: no declared box'; this lane measured it in a browser.
accessibility.$notLive: ⛔ THE CONTROLS ON THESE PAGES LOOK LIVE AND ARE NOT. Nothing sorts, filters, pages or switches tabs. Each page is drawn in ONE real resting state. That is deliberate (see antiPatterns) and it is the single most likely thing for a reviewer to misread.

antiPatterns: Do not re-draw an atom inside a template. If a region here diverges from its source component, that is a defect, not a variant — the #202 lesson (three hand-rolled specimen pages, three invented defects).
Do not give a molecule inside a template a fixed width. s210-D3: the container dictates the width. A TEMPLATE may declare page-level layout width because it IS the container; nothing inside it may.

Do not host a source component's JavaScript engine here. Sorting, filtering, paging, tab switching, chart fitting and legend filtering belong to Data-grid, Pagination, Tabs and Chart-bar. Copying an engine into a template forks it, and a fork drifts silently.

Do not copy a source component's raw `font:` declaration. Every one of them feeds the 1,097 TYPE-002 debt, which is shrink-only. Borrow the geometry and the colour; bind type with a .t-cm-* / .t-ed-* class in the markup.

⛔ Do not assume a `@container` rule you copied will fire. `container-type` makes an element a container for its DESCENDANTS, never for itself. Measured at #210: without a host, Layout-utilities' `.l-split` stayed two columns at 420px and its content column measured 26px, with every gate green.

⛔ Do not assume a copied `text-box-edge: text text` override wins. Measured at #210: the single-class form computes `cap alphabetic` and clips 3.88px of every descender, because the canon trim rule's `:is()` list contains attribute selectors and therefore weighs 0-1-2. Use the two-class form AND measure the computed edge (ds-005).
⛔ Do not namespace a borrowed rule without re-checking what used to beat it. Scoping `th,td` to `.dg th,.dg td` raised it from 0-0-1 to 0-1-1 and silently un-centred the borrowed `.dg-empty` panel.
Do not invent a domain semantic. Every status word, column, facet and section order on these pages is PROPOSED (s182-D2) and is Dave's.

provenance.$sourceNarrative: Itinerary row 104 ('Template — dashboard', layer '2 Template', priority P2, notes 'Composes from stat/chart/grid bases.', derived NO-ARTEFACT-CLASS) in reviews/ITINERARY-STATUS-2026-08-19-v1.json

$foundByLooking: ⛔ THE SPLIT NEVER COLLAPSED. Layout-utilities' `.l-split` puts `container-type:inline-size` on ITSELF, but a `@container` rule resolves against an element's nearest ANCESTOR container and an element is never its own — so the collapse rule can never match. Measured: this page at 420px had a 26px chart stage and a 26px paragraph; the GATED PARENT at 1400px computes `90px 280px` inside its own 394px demo frame while its caption claims it 'has already collapsed'; at 420px the parent's top-level split computes `44px 280px`. MUTATION CONTROL: adding `container-type` to the split's PARENT gives `394px`, one column. Repaired here with a composition host; the parent's repair is REPORTED, not applied.

⛔ THE CHART BARS RENDERED SOLID BLACK, IN BOTH THEMES, WITH EVERY GATE GREEN. The column specimen fills every rect with `var(--data-series-1)`; the theme blocks carried only `--data-series-3`, left over from the h-bar specimen it replaced. `fill:var(--undefined)` falls back to the SVG initial value, BLACK, in silence. This is [[dangling-dataviz-var-renders-silent-black]] (#184) reproduced at COMPOSITION time — a template inherits a var contract from every component it composes and nothing checks that it carried them all. A dangling-var probe was written, driven, and MUTATION-CONTROLLED (healthy: 0 dangling, fill rgb(118,102,130); mutated: 1 dangling, fill rgb(0,0,0)).
The chart panel stretched to the rail's height and rendered ~230px of empty card. Repaired with `align-items:start` (composition rule 13).
$layerNote: ⚠ THE BRIEF ASKS FOR A `layer` FIELD; THE SCHEMA FORBIDS IT, AND THE SCHEMA WINS. meta.schema.json allows only `$`-prefixed additional root keys, so the itinerary's layer value is carried as `$layer`. Declared rather than smuggled: if Dave wants a first-class `layer` field for the Layer-2 artefact class, that is a SCHEMA change and is his, not a worker lane's.
$composesNote: ⚠ `relationships` is a CLOSED shape in meta.schema.json (livesInside · mustNotNeighbour · commonPatterns · triggeredBy) and has no seat for 'the components this organism is assembled from'. ⬛ THAT IS A REAL GAP FOR LAYER 2 and it is named, not worked around silently: composition is the defining edge of a template, and the graph cannot currently express it. The list is carried as `$composes` so it is readable and greppable but does not pretend to be a graph edge. Adding a `composes` edge type is a schema change and is Dave's.
